source_references.title: Mustang Machinery’s digital service coach: PwC

business_problem: Mustang Machinery needed to serve growing heavy-equipment demand during a labor shortage by standardizing maintenance work, preserving expert knowledge, and giving technicians faster guidance on the shop floor.
solution_summary: Mustang Machinery combined low-code apps, analytics, and generative AI to address a skilled-labor shortage without slowing engine maintenance. PwC first documented 60,000 process steps across engine rebuild activities, parts requirements, and shop-floor visuals, then built a digital service coach on Microsoft Power Platform. PowerApps delivers a mobile workflow interface to technicians, Dataverse stores operational data, and Power BI exposes planning and scheduling insights in real time. The solution also includes a generative AI chatbot that serves information from the growing knowledgebase so technicians can retrieve answers quickly instead of waiting on experts. Together, these components create a single source of truth for workstation setup, parts availability, maintenance guidance, and support escalation. Mustang can now coordinate work across multiple sites with just-in-time upskilling, real-time visibility, and faster decision-making.

data_flow: Process steps, parts requirements, visuals, and shop-floor updates flow into Dataverse through the PowerApps-based digital service coach. Power BI serves planning and scheduling views, while the generative AI chatbot queries the knowledgebase to return guidance and answers to technicians and support staff in real time.
business_outcome: Mustang increased throughput 2.5x, put standardized guidance in front of more than 100 technicians, and reduced dependency on tribal knowledge while scaling service operations across multiple sites.
metrics: 60,000 process steps analyzed, standardized and captured to create a new way of working supported by the new digital solution
100+ technicians using the solution across a network of multiple production sites

Microsoft’s Power Platform enabled us to go from concept to full-scale deployment in three months.
architecture_clues: PwC captured 60,000 process steps and visuals through shop-floor shadowing.
PowerApps, Dataverse, and Power BI run inside Mustang’s existing Microsoft environment.
The chatbot serves answers from the technician knowledgebase in real time.
The digital service coach supports just-in-time guidance and support-tech escalation across multiple sites.
evidence_quotes: Using its Manufacturing Performance Improvement framework, PwC first standardized detailed engine rebuild processes. It then leveraged our existing Microsoft environment to build a cost-effective solution using Microsoft Power Platform: PowerApps for development of the digital services coach solution, Dataverse for data storage and management, and Power BI for data analytics and visualization of planning and scheduling information.
The solution also has a generative AI-based chatbot that provides another way to quickly serve up info needed from the vast knowledgebase.
